enso.cpc_discussion: ENSO Alert System Status: El Niño Advisory   Synopsis:   El Niño continues to strengthen, with a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027 (remaining greater than an 83% chance). El Niño strengthened further last month, with sea surface temperature anomalies exceeding +4.0°C in portions of the eastern equatorial Pacific [Fig. 1] . Most Niño indices increased in the past month, reaching +2.1°C in Niño-3.4, +3.0°C in Niño-3, and +3.9°C in Niño-1+2 [Fig. 2] . The equatorial subsurface temperature index (average from 180°-100°W) was well above average [Fig. 3] , reflecting a deeper-than-average thermocline. Subsurface temperatures remained in excess of +10.0°C at depth in the eastern Pacific Ocean [Fig. 4] . Low-level westerly wind anomalies and upper-level easterly wind anomalies stretched from the western to the east-central equatorial Pacific. Enhanced convection and rainfall persisted from the central to the eastern Pacific, while anomalies remained suppressed over Indonesia [Fig. 5] . The traditional and equatorial Southern Oscillation indices were significantly negative. Collectively, the coupled ocean-atmosphere system reflected a strengthening El Niño. The CPC Official ENSO outlook , which synthesizes multiple models from North America and abroad, indicates El Niño will continue to strengthen through the end of the year [Figs. 6 -7 -8] . notes: Wind/gust ranges: quantile-boosted models widened by a conformal margin fit on out-of-fold errors (days 1-10 ensemble model).

Temperature ranges: NBM high/low plus the empirical error distribution (by lead day and season) measured at Alamogordo, Holloman and Las Cruces airports; the same error spread is assumed at Hawk St, the Pass and Cloudcroft (mountain sites are not verified).
Rain: percentile amounts come from the hurdle model; coverage above nominal mostly reflects the large share of dry days. Cloudcroft days 8-10 slightly under-cover (88% vs 90%).
Test period: Jul 2025 – Oct 2026 (about 15 months), so coverage numbers carry a few points of sampling noise.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service El Paso TX/Santa Teresa NM
1019 PM MDT Sun Oct 18 2026

...New DISCUSSION, AVIATION...

.KEY MESSAGES... Updated at 1019 PM MDT Sun Oct 18 2026

 - Low rain chances through Wednesday, favoring western areas.

 - Better areawide rain chances Thursday and Friday, with some 
strong storms and flooding possible.

 - Temperatures back above normal, with Tuesday through Thursday 
being the warmest stretch.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 1019 PM MDT Sun Oct 18 2026

WV imagery showing mid-level (500mb) low over far SW Arizona and 
continuing to slowly drift northeast. Deeper layered moisture 
remains north and southeast of the CWA, with less layered moisture 
over the CWA. That said, KEPZ sounding shows most moisture sitting 
between 700mb and 500mb, while dewpoints are back into the lower 40s 
most places. So some light showers continue across southern portions 
of our forecast area this evening. Modest instability down over 
northern Mexico has allowed a few thunderstorms to develop in that 
area. As they drift northeast toward our southern CWA, they appear 
to weaken to just a few showers. 

Monday and Tuesday...sub-tropical jet increases in strength and 
approaches New Mexico from the southwest. Models showing one leading 
jetlet from the main jet moving over southern New Mexico through 
Tuesday. Also the main trough from the Arizona low nears the AZ/NM 
state line later Monday as the parent low lifts out over the Four 
Corners. This added large scale lift will combine with PWs mostly 
unchanged from today, and dewpoints increasing to mid to upper 40s, 
to aid in isolated to scattered showers and thunderstorms both days. 
Coverage may lessen some on Tuesday with slight drying aloft and the 
upper trough passage.  

Wednesday and Thursday...next large Pacific low approaches SoCal 
Wednesday night and 90+ kt sub-tropical jet moves over western New 
Mexico by Thursday. This will draw sub-tropical moisture over 
central Mexico northward to the area, perhaps including some 
moisture from Trudy. Max PWs occur from Wednesday night through 
Thursday night, approaching 1.2 inches, which is well over 200% of 
normal. Thus expect good shower/thunderstorm coverage to develop 
Wednesday afternoon. It could very well last much of the overnight 
hours and continue much of Thursday. MUCAPES of 300-600 J/kg along 
with decent veering profile, show decent potential for some strong 
storms. Main threat though could be local heavy rainfall and 
flooding. 

Friday through Sunday...Friday looks to begin transition down as the 
main upper trough lifts across the area. Areas from the RG Valley 
east could still see decent coverage of showers/storms, but should 
taper off to the west. From there the GFS/ECMWF continue to diverge 
significantly in solutions. The GFS continues to break off secondary 
low over the northern Baja Saturday and Sunday, keeping sub-tropical 
moisture and widespread showers again by Sunday. The ECMWF is much 
more progressive, with little or no secondary low development. Thus, 
area should remain dry, though ECMWF does begin moving moisture back 
in after this period. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(06Z TAFS) Issued at 1019 PM MDT Sun Oct 18 2026

VFR conditions through the period with SCT080 SCT-BKN200. Isolated 
BKN060 -SHRA, mainly from Deming-Alamogordo south. These showers 
should dissipate next 3-6 hours. Developing after 18Z mainly west
of the RG Valley...isolated OVC050CB -TSRA. Thunderstorms moving 
to east of the RG Valley late Monday afternoon into the evening. 
Winds variable AOB 7 knots becoming south/southeast 7-10 knots 
after 18Z. TAF sites could see thunderstorms after 21Z, but not 
enough confidence yet to include in the TAFs. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
Issued at 1130 AM MDT Sun Oct 18 2026

Fire weather concerns will remain low through the period as moisture 
returns to the area. A few showers and thunderstorms are possible, 
especially western half of the area through early in the week. A 
stronger storm system moves into the west later in the week and will 
bring more widespread rain to the region.
Temperatures will be warming into the mid 70s to mid 80s through 
Wednesday with RH's remaining above 25% with light winds. Cooler 
temps and higher RH's for late in the week. Vent rates the next 
couple of days will be Poor east to Good west on Mon and improving 
to Good to Very good on Tue. 

&&
